description: Ratified 2026-10-21. IMP-6 (coordinator-decisions-ruling-round-2.md, D-22): an act with no matching act_signed event is anomalous. Not built yet.

T-459 AC3 (mutate the comparison, confirm a test fails) -- THIS IS WHERE IT BREAKS. Mutant A: changed the match/anomalous branch in imp6_check to always append to matched (skip the key-membership check). Result: 4 of 15 tests fail (test_an_act_with_no_matching_event_is_anomalous, test_a_different_seq_does_not_accidentally_match, test_only_act_signed_events_are_counted_not_every_event_kind, EpicCloseWrapsThreeAndNeverGates::test_a_fork_and_an_orphan_and_an_anomalous_act_all_present_exit_stays_0). Caught, as expected.

Mutant B (cognitive-diversity probe, different angle): replaced the single line `ident = event_stats.identity(e)` in _signed_event_keys with an inline reimplementation `ident = (e.get('ts'), e.get('name'))` -- i.e. a silent regression that keeps the `import event_stats` line (so the existing identity-pin test `test_the_dedup_predicate_is_imported_from_event_stats_not_reimplemented`, which only asserts `cc.event_stats.identity is event_stats.identity`, still passes) but stops calling the ratified D-9 predicate at the actual call site. Full result: `python3 -m pytest .harness/tests/test_close_checks.py -q` -> 15 passed, 0 failed. This mutant is NOT caught by any test.

Why this matters and is not a nitpick: it breaks exactly the guarantee the module's own docstring claims ("this tool cannot drift from the ratified predicate by having its own slightly-different copy") and exactly the TELEMETRY-PROVENANCE-A scenario M-1 exists to catch (raw count overstating distinct). Root cause found by reading the fixture: `_write_event()`'s default `ts` is a FIXED constant ("2026-10-21T00:00:01Z"), and `test_replayed_events_collapse_to_one_distinct_but_raw_stays_high` -- the one test meant to pin D-9 -- never overrides it, so all 3 "duplicate" events in that test share one identical ts. A dedup that wrongly includes ts in its identity key is therefore indistinguishable, to this suite, from one that correctly excludes it, because the test fixture never actually varies ts between duplicates. Confirmed independently with varying real ts values in a throwaway root: under mutant B, raw=5 distinct=5 (should be distinct=1) while the printed label still claims "two events are identical when they agree on every field except 'ts'" -- the report lies about what it computed. Match/anomaly output was unaffected in this specific case (set membership on (name,seq) still worked), but the raw/distinct reporting half of AC1 silently breaks and no test in the suite notices.

Fix needed before this can go to done: in test_replayed_events_collapse_to_one_distinct_but_raw_stays_high (or a new test), vary ts across the duplicate _write_event calls (pass ts=... explicitly per call) so a dedup that incorrectly keys on ts is actually caught. No other acceptance criterion failed. Replay, in a throwaway copy under the session scratchpad (never in the working tree; close_checks.py/test_close_checks.py in the live repo were not touched):
  python3 -m pytest .harness/tests/test_close_checks.py -q -k "not RealClis"  (RealClis needs the live repo root, deselected for the isolated copy)
  baseline: 12 passed, 4 deselected
  after applying mutant C: 12 passed, 4 deselected -- UNCAUGHT, 0 failures.

And it is not merely a reporting nitpick -- it produces an actively WRONG anomaly verdict, which is exactly what IMP-6 exists to prevent. Direct demonstration (two genuinely different, properly act_signed acts for ONE agent name, different seq -- the ordinary case, not a corner case):
  write_act("orso", 7); write_act("orso", 8)
  write_event(name="orso", seq=7, ...); write_event(name="orso", seq=8, ...)
  cc.imp6_check(root) under mutant C ->
    act_signed_events: raw=2, distinct=1   (should be distinct=2 -- these are two different acts, not a replay duplicate)
    acts_matched=1, acts_anomalous=[{"name":"orso","seq":8,...}]

Act orso#8 WAS properly signed (its event is on disk) but is reported ANOMALOUS, because the coarser dedup key treats the seq=7 event as having "already been seen" under name "orso" and silently drops the seq=8 event out of the matched-keys set before matching ever runs. The bug is not confined to the raw/distinct counters M-1 cares about; it corrupts `acts_anomalous` itself -- a false positive on a legitimately-signed act, for the single most ordinary scenario the module has to handle (one agent, multiple acts). None of the 16 tests construct this case: every "collapse to distinct=1" test in the suite (including both new round-2 tests) reuses the SAME act (same name AND seq) for every duplicate event, and every "do not accidentally match" test uses a DIFFERENT name. No test has two different real acts sharing a name with different seq and distinct, real act_signed events for each.

This is not the same gap round 2 was asked to close (that one was ts-inclusion, a too-fine key); this is the opposite failure mode at the identical call site (a too-coarse key), and the module's own docstring claim ("this tool cannot drift from the ratified predicate by having its own slightly-different copy") is still false for this mutant.

Fix needed before this can go to done: add a test with two distinct real acts (same name, different seq, or same seq different name -- anything that actually varies more than one field while reusing another) each with its own act_signed event, and assert raw==2, distinct==2, both matched, neither anomalous. A single parametrized case covering "two different acts sharing a name" would close both the under- and over-collapse failure modes at once.
